Correct for the file; wrong as the input to a repo-wide question, which is the use it actually gets. **Not fixed in this pass, and the reason is specific:** `resolveStartPhase` (`drive.js:580`) detects the resume path with `candidate?.source?.includes('STATE.md')`, so a cross-branch candidate fed through it would resume an Epic **on the wrong branch** — the fix has to decide whether `/sig:drive` may check out a branch, which is a design call and not a papercut. **Fix shapes, none chosen:** (a) enumerate `refs/remotes/origin/*`, read each `STATE.md`, surface any unshipped `current_epic` differing from the local one as a candidate **carrying its branch name**, and make `resolveStartPhase` refuse rather than resume when the candidate's branch is not the current one; (b) the minimum honest version, which costs almost nothing and can ship first — push `{source: 'STATE.md on other branches', reason: 'N remote branches carry a STATE.md this reader did not open'}` into `cannotCheck`, so the empty-and-clean read stops being indistinguishable from a complete one. **(b) alone would have surfaced this**, and `drive.md` already forbids presenting an unread source as an empty result. ⚠ **WIDER THAN FILED: `/sig:advise` has the same blindness, and the PR reviewer on `#248` found it — in the fix for this very row.** `readCorpus` (`advise-corpus.js`) resolves every one of its five sources as `join(baseDir, …)`; it makes **no** git call and enumerates **no** branch, so all five are read from whichever branch is checked out. The reviewer's route in was not the code but the prose: this PR's own `CLAUDE.md` paragraph established that `M6.E8` is invisible to tooling and then **closed by telling the reader to run `/sig:advise`, which exists to answer that** — pointing at the failure mode two sentences after describing it. **So the fix does not belong in `drive.js`.** Both commands answer *"what should I work on"* from a one-branch read, and shape (b) has to land in the shared corpus layer or it fixes one caller and leaves the other. That also means the blast radius is every consumer of `readCorpus`, not just the driver. **Fresh sighting 2026-09-14 (`M6.E8` VERIFY):** the Epic's own Outcome procedure — *"diff the next advisory against `BACKLOG-REVIEW-2026-09-13.md`"* — is invalid **because of this bug**. The baseline was generated on `main` (`46e6e44`) and lacks the row this branch promoted at DISCUSS (`7e9c288`), so the diff measures corpus drift plus ranking change and cannot separate them; run literally it shows the recommended five changing, which is false. A controlled experiment on one corpus gives an identical top five. **So this bug does not only pick the wrong work — it silently invalidates advisory-to-advisory comparison**, which is the only outcome instrument the corpus offers. |
| SIG-119 | `confirmed` | P3 | **`/sig:advise`'s artifact carries no commit anchor, so its `path:line` citations are true at exactly one commit and nothing in the file says which.** `ADHERENCE-LOG.md` pins the producing SHA for exactly this reason (AC4.3); `renderArtifact` writes none. Observed 2026-09-13: `BACKLOG-REVIEW-2026-09-13.md` was generated at `46e6e44`; merging `main` into `feat/m6.e8-advisor-ranking-inputs` brought a 22-line row in at `BACKLOG.md:95`, and every citation from line 95 on is now off by 23 on that branch while `verifyCitations` would still pass them all — the limit the `M6.E7` retro records for the 2026-09-06 artifact, now reached by ordinary drift rather than a SHIP edit. Fix: write the generating `HEAD` into the artifact's *Corpus read* section, so a reader can `git show <sha>:.planning/BACKLOG.md` and the citations resolve again. Fits `M6.E8` if PLAN takes it; otherwise a fix-lane row. **Fresh sighting 2026-09-14 (`M6.E8` VERIFY):** a **second** unanchored artifact now exists — `BACKLOG-REVIEW-2026-09-14.md`, 53 citations true at `60b9f1f` and nowhere else. Produced by the Epic that read the bug, which is the argument for fixing it in the renderer rather than noting it in each artifact. |
| SIG-120 | `fixed` | P3 | **`tests/drain-standing.test.js` AC2.2c pins THIS repo's `ISSUES-INBOX.md` at zero live candidates, so every `/sig:add` to the inbox turns the suite red until the next `/sig:plan` drain disposes of the entry.** The assertion reads the live file (`listDrainCandidates(inbox)).toHaveLength(0)`) as *"the measurable outcome from M6.E4-REQUIREMENTS.md"* — true on 2026-08-19 and a snapshot ever since. Reproduced 2026-09-14: filing the tier-drift row from `/sig:resume` at `M6.E8` PLAN entry (`D-BR0914-1`) made it the only failure in 3381 tests, on correct behaviour. This is the *"ceiling on an append-only ledger"* shape the house rules name: a check that fires when the ledger is used teaches people to ignore the check, and the window it fires in is exactly the one where a capture is supposed to sit — between a capture and the drain that reads it. Fix shape: assert what `M6.E4` actually delivered — that the standing entry is excluded and that every *dispositioned* entry (`→ Deferred`, `→ Promoted`, …) leaves the live count — rather than that the count is zero; or pin the count at zero only against a committed fixture. Fix lane; not `M6.E8`'s. |
| SIG-121 | `fixed` | P2 | **`parseBacklogRows` returns ZERO rows for a CRLF `BACKLOG.md`, and `/sig:advise` then writes an advisory saying *"Nothing. No live row survived the ranking inputs."*** `headingRe` is `/^(#{2,4})\s+(.*)$/` with **no `m` flag**, so `$` matches only at end of input and `.` excludes `\r`: a heading line ending in `\r` never matches. Measured: the same file at LF yields 2 rows, at CRLF **0**. A Windows checkout with `core.autocrlf=true` produces exactly this file. **The consequence reaches the citation gate:** zero rows means zero claims, `verifyCitations` returns `ok` over nothing, `0 >= 0` passes, and the artifact is written. `advise.js`'s own docblock reasons that *"`claims === 0` implies `rows.length === 0`, and with no live rows there is genuinely nothing to cite"* — **false for this input: 52 rows exist and 0 were parsed.** `walkBugEntries` DOES parse CRLF, so the same artifact still claims `BUGS.md` was consulted. Found by the `M6.E8` REVIEW pass-3 security audit, reproduced. Fix: split on `/\r?\n/` (or strip a trailing `\r`) in `parseBacklogRows`, and have `readCorpus` report cannot-check when the file has bytes but zero headings at any depth. |
| SIG-122 | `fixed` | P2 | **The `<details>` counter in `parseBacklogRows` is fence-unaware and code-span-unaware, so any MENTION of `<details` silently drops every row after it.** `inFence` gates `headingRe` but the depth counter accumulates on every line, including inside fenced blocks and inline code spans. Measured: a fenced ```` ```\n<details>\n``` ```` block and an inline `` `<details>` `` mention each mark the FOLLOWING live row `inDetails: true`; `readCorpus` filters those rows out of `live` with **no `cannotCheck`**, so they appear in neither the recommended nor the declined list — while the artifact states the declined pool is *"complete rather than curated"*. Also blinds `backlogDischargeStatus` to those rows and makes `dischargeBacklogRows` report `not-found` for a row that exists. **Zero such mentions on this repository today**, so it is latent here and live for any project whose backlog discusses `<details>`. Found by the `M6.E8` REVIEW pass-3 security audit, reproduced. Fix: skip the counting inside fences and strip code spans first, or anchor on `^\s*<details` / `^\s*</details>` as block openers. |

The pass-3 security audit probed it read-only and reports that traversals out of `.planning/` are **refused** by that guard, but that a stamp of `/../archive/x` is **allowed** and would write the advisory into `.planning/archive/` instead of the planning root. ⚠ **Filed as `needs-triage` rather than `confirmed` because the author's own re-probe was inconclusive** — it refused every stamp including the valid one, which means the probe did not reproduce the auditor's setup rather than that the finding is wrong.
